newsitem.title: USA: Russia warns NATO not to lure in ex-Soviet states.
newsitem.headline: Russia warns NATO not to lure in ex-Soviet states.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Saturday Moscow would review relations with NATO if the Western defence alliance offered membership to former Soviet republics.

"If NATO really expands at the expense of former Soviet republics, it will force us to look again at the whole system of relations with NATO," Primakov told a news conference at the summit of the Group of Seven industrial nations.

Russia remains opposed to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's plans to expand into former communist eastern Europe, despite signing a partnership deal with its former Cold War foe in May which eased some of its concerns.
Moscow has said repeatedly that it would not accept any attempts by NATO to lure in former outposts of the Soviet Union, a move which it regards as a threat to its security.
The repetition of these concerns at the G7 summit was a sober reminder that a problem divides Moscow and most G7 members, despite Russia's deepening integration with the elite club.
Russia is particularly concerned that NATO might offer membership to the Baltic states of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia and to its fellow Slav neighbour Ukraine.
